title: 1995 AHSME Problem 16
statement:
Anita attends a baseball game in Atlanta and estimates that there are \(50{,}000\) fans in attendance. Bob attends a baseball game in Boston and estimates that there are \(60{,}000\) fans in attendance. A league official who knows the actual numbers attending the two games notes that:

i. The actual attendance in Atlanta is within \(10\%\) of Anita’s estimate.

ii. Bob’s estimate is within \(10\%\) of the actual attendance in Boston.

To the nearest \(1{,}000,\) the largest possible difference between the numbers attending the two games is

solutions.text: Atlanta’s actual attendance \(A\) satisfies \(45{,}000\le A\le55{,}000.\) For Boston’s actual attendance \(B,\) the condition is \(|60{,}000-B|\le0.1B,\) so \(\frac{60{,}000}{1.1}\le B\le\frac{60{,}000}{0.9}.\) The largest difference is therefore \[ \frac{60{,}000}{0.9}-45{,}000 =21{,}666.\overline6, \] which rounds to \(22{,}000.\) Thus the correct answer is E.
hints: In the two statements, the \(10\%\) is taken of different quantities
Find both attendance intervals, then maximize the larger endpoint minus the smaller endpoint
